scope: Experimental physical-interpretation conventions. Raster container formats have their own specifications.

conventions.definition: The boundary break and the unequal two marks identify the start corner. The larger mark precedes the smaller along the first row axis.
conventions.observation: Orient unfamiliar, rotated and mirrored sheets using the markers, then point to the first usable position.

conventions.definition: A bounded cell contains either a dark inset or no inset. Separately learn which numerical or image state it denotes.
conventions.observation: Recover the same cell sequence on different readable replicas and flag ambiguous or missing marks.

conventions.definition: An isolated dot precedes the regularly spaced cells and a bar ends the sequence.
conventions.observation: Separate two adjacent sequences without counting the delimiter as a data cell.

conventions.definition: The number of marks inside a quantity boundary is counted. No mark inside the boundary represents zero.
conventions.observation: Pair a new arrangement of marks with the matching quantity and identify the empty case.

conventions.definition: A dark inset contributes the position's weight. The last position has weight one. Each preceding position doubles the weight.
conventions.observation: Interpret a longer held-out group whose value differs from the count of inset cells.

conventions.definition: Repeated dot-group relations pair glyphs with equality, order, operations, signed groups and an unknown.
conventions.observation: Complete a held-out relation without the examples sharing its outcome.

conventions.definition: Count intervals relative to a common origin or equal-pitch reference. A proportional scaling preserves ratios of lengths.
conventions.observation: Place a new coordinate and compare two similar diagrams using length ratios.

conventions.definition: Candidate period and vacuum wavelength come from the rest-frame neutral protium ground-state hyperfine transition.
conventions.observation: Distinguish the two quantities and name the transition; C1 does not yet teach its full experimental identification.

conventions.definition: Start at the marked corner, cross each row along the first axis, and then move one row along the second axis.
conventions.observation: Recover asymmetric grids and reject alternative transposed or reversed interpretations.

conventions.definition: The toy frames pair dimensions, identifier, mode and sample count with a row-grouped payload. Monochrome open becomes dark; filled becomes light. Other toy modes use increasing intensity codes or ordered RGB triplets.
conventions.observation: Agree on header values and independently reconstruct held-out monochrome, grayscale and color results.

conventions.definition: A large four-position tag occurs on the outer map and on its matching target outline. The tag identifies a region; payload cells sit inside the region.
conventions.observation: Select a target by a new tag among alternatives, independent of target order.

conventions.definition: Pairs show the same target geometry at two pitches. Enlarging every distance by four preserves state, order, relative position and number of cells.
conventions.observation: Predict a matching enlarged shape and record the fine-to-coarse pitch ratio.

conventions.definition: Independently orient the selected tile by its notch and two marks. Read its cells in groups across rows without changing state. Unresolved cells are recorded as unknown.
conventions.observation: Recover an unseen fine tile and its locator. Separately record region, orientation, pitch inference, cell agreement and missing states.
